hazards.reason: Copying order, order_label and order_line holds the database's write lock for time that grows with the tables.
hazards.subject: table/order

hazards.reason: SQLite's ALTER TABLE cannot change foreign key fk_order_customer_id, so the step rebuilds order with the tables that reference it, directly or through another table: order_label and order_line. It copies the rows of each table it keeps into a new table, drops the old tables and renames the new ones.
hazards.subject: table/order

statements:
CREATE TABLE "_new_order" (
  "id" TEXT DEFAULT (lower(hex(randomblob(4)) || '-' || hex(randomblob(2)) || '-4' || substr(hex(randomblob(2)), 2) || '-' || substr('89ab', 1 + (random() & 3), 1) || substr(hex(randomblob(2)), 2) || '-' || hex(randomblob(6)))) NOT NULL,
  "code" TEXT NOT NULL,
  "customer_id" TEXT NOT NULL,
  "total" INTEGER NOT NULL,
  "reference" TEXT,
  "note" TEXT,
  "placed_at" TEXT NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY ("id"),
  FOREIGN KEY ("customer_id") REFERENCES "customer" ("id") ON DELETE CASCADE
)

CREATE TABLE "_new_order_label" (
  "order_id" TEXT NOT NULL,
  "label_id" TEXT NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY ("order_id", "label_id"),
  FOREIGN KEY ("label_id") REFERENCES "label" ("id") ON DELETE CASCADE,
  FOREIGN KEY ("order_id") REFERENCES "_new_order" ("id") ON DELETE CASCADE
)

CREATE TABLE "_new_order_line" (
  "id" TEXT DEFAULT (lower(hex(randomblob(4)) || '-' || hex(randomblob(2)) || '-4' || substr(hex(randomblob(2)), 2) || '-' || substr('89ab', 1 + (random() & 3), 1) || substr(hex(randomblob(2)), 2) || '-' || hex(randomblob(6)))) NOT NULL,
  "sku" TEXT NOT NULL,
  "quantity" INTEGER NOT NULL,
  "order_id" TEXT NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY ("id"),
  FOREIGN KEY ("order_id") REFERENCES "_new_order" ("id") ON DELETE CASCADE
)
steps.subject: table/order
